safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated contains no statement about haemodynamic stability.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In a patient with suspected acute coronary syndrome, noting haemodynamic stability helps downstream triage and conveys immediate risk (e.g., shock/instability) to EMS/ED. Omission may reduce clarity of urgency/acuity in handover, though EMS will reassess vitals on arrival.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the patient was examined seated at rest is a contextual documentation detail and does not meaningfully change diagnosis or immediate management in this scenario. EMS/ED evaluation will be based on real-time vitals and examination.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated contains no statement about being well perfused on video inspection.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting that the patient appears well perfused on video can help communicate absence of overt shock/poor perfusion during remote assessment. Its omission may slightly degrade the quality of clinical handover but is unlikely to change immediate care because perfusion will be reassessed promptly by EMS.

safety_verdicts.content: Urgent ECG and troponin T are required.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions ECG but does not mention urgent troponin T testing.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Troponin testing is a core component of suspected myocardial infarction/ACS evaluation and helps guide diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment decisions. Omitting the need for urgent troponin may contribute to incomplete or delayed diagnostic workup if relied upon in handover/documentation.

safety_verdicts.content: Ambulance (LAS) was called with blue lights.
